subject: Marketplace listing credit structure and co-marketing allowance discussion

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, James Liu <james.liu@amazon.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Q1 credit allowance + listing fee conversation

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the call last week. As we discussed, SigmaCloud is preparing the Q1 marketplace playbook and we'd like to align on the listing credit allowance and co-marketing credit schedule for Redwood's AWS listing renewal. Attached is a proposed schedule that shows a modest increase in listing credits tied to commit thresholds.

Key asks from our side:
- Maintain 60% listing-fee waiver for the first 90 days post-listing;
- Increase co-marketing credit from $25k to $40k if Redwood commits to a joint webinar and 3 case studies;
- Clarify the reporting cadence for credit drawdown and proof points.

Attachment: Proposed_Credit_Schedule_Q1-2027.pdf (1 page)

Can you confirm who on your team will own acceptance and whether there are any internal approval gates we should be aware of? James from AWS is looped to confirm any platform-side constraints.

Best,
Elyse Carter
Head of Partnerships, SigmaCloud
elyse@sigmacloud.com

Team — forwarding Elyse's note (below). Quick context: SigmaCloud is proposing a bumped co-marketing credit in exchange for joint demand-generation activities and a slightly higher listing-fee waiver early in the term. We need to decide: do we accept the dollar amounts as-is, push for a stronger listing-fee waiver, or trade additional product-level commitments for credits?

Questions:
1) Marcus — negotiation levers (co-marketing vs. listing fee waiver) — what gives us the most cost-efficient customer reach?
2) Karthik/Laura — any procurement or finance constraints for committing to a co-marketing guarantee (webinar + case studies)? Approval timeline?
3) Should we ask for a 12-month cap on partner credit usage to prevent unexpected drawdowns?

I attached the proposal from Elyse. Please reply with quick takes; I'll consolidate and get a counter together by Tuesday.

Priya — thanks for the forward. Short take: prioritize an extended listing-fee waiver for the initial window (we want early visibility in the marketplace search and sponsoring placements). Co-marketing dollars are helpful but harder to guarantee ROI unless SigmaCloud commits to joint lead handling.

Suggested counter (high level):
- Maintain 60% listing-fee waiver for first 120 days (instead of 90);
- Offer $35k co-marketing credit with joint GTM milestones (webinar + 2 case studies + shared demand gen asset) rather than unconditional $40k;
- Cap annual partner credit usage to $50k unless we escalate to VP approval.

I attached an updated terms draft that rephrases the credit drawdown and adds a cap. See Marketplace_Terms_v3.docx. If we need to sweeten, we can offer a product feature spot in our upcoming release notes (low-cost to us, high-signal to customers).

- Marcus
VP, Business Development
Redwood Inference

+1 on Marcus's suggested counter. From procurement/finance perspective:
- We can sign up to a $35k co-marketing credit but need to ensure the payment/credit realization schedule maps to MRR recognition rules — Laura, can you confirm if we need a PO or any special SOW language?
- Approval timeline: standard channel for partner marketing spend is 7-10 business days assuming no legal redlines. If Elyse's team requires a longer-term cap, route to finance for VP sign-off.

If Priya wants, I'll draft a procurement note for consolidation.

Karthik Iyer

Hi Elyse — thanks for the proposal and for looping James. Apologies for the slightly slow turnaround; I wanted to align with our internal stakeholders.

We can move forward on the following counter-proposal:
- Listing-fee waiver: 60% for the first 120 days post-listing (aligns to Marcus's ask);
- Co-marketing credit: $35,000 contingent on agreed milestones (webinar, 2 customer case studies, and a shared demand-gen asset).
- Annual partner credit cap: $50,000 unless escalated to our VP of Partnerships for approval.
- Reporting cadence: monthly drawdown reports; quarterly review for credit usage.

If this looks acceptable, please confirm and I will:
1) send a tailored MOA for signature (DocuSign link included once terms are agreed);
2) connect our marketing ops to coordinate webinar timelines; and
3) share the credit reporting template.

Forwarding our internal terms draft for reference. Attachment: DocuSign_MOA_v2.pdf (stub for MOA).
